summary: ```markdown # Marvelous Designer: Half-Skirt Production Tutorial - Pumpkin Skirt In this video, we will learn how to make a pumpkin skirt. ## Step 1: Preparing the Skirt First, we freeze the belt and then delete the excess outer layer, that is, the outer layer of the cake skirt. We only keep the inner layer. After a simple simulation, we select the bottom and add elasticity to it; it will automatically close. After closing, we can reduce the proportion a little bit to check if it is tight. After tightening, it looks like a pumpkin skirt. ## Step 2: Adding Pressure Next, we can select these plates to add pressure. Because the bottom is tight, we add pressure to it. This will help the skirt hold up. Once it holds up, it will look more obvious and resemble a pumpkin skirt. If you feel that the pressure is too strong when it is set to 2, you can adjust the pressure to 0.5. Click on the triangle on the left to reduce the pressure. ## Step 3: Adjusting Elasticity Since we used elasticity, the bottom of our skirt is fixed and cannot move up or down. Many times, the bottom of the skirt may appear more obvious, so we need to adjust it. We can cancel the elasticity first, then activate the outer layer of the plate. ## Step 4: Fixing the Skirt We first fix the belt to the bottom of the skirt. Change to the rectangular tool and adjust it to the position we think is appropriate. For example, if I click on it, I think this position is about right, just around this tight position. We will create an almost three times wider leg or 2.5 times wider rectangle. ### Creating a Symmetrical Plate Next, we create a symmetrical plate. Continue to select these two plates simultaneously. After selecting a plate, click Shift again to select more. Then, press Shift + F to open the arrangement point and arrange them in the front position. After adjusting the diameter, you can close the arrangement point. If the arrangement position is slightly crossed or needs adjustment, we will manually use the positioning ball to adjust it. ## Step 5: Sewing the Plates After arranging, use the satin sewing machine to sew the two ends together. Since the entire plate is relatively small, we can click on the display grid to see that the number of grids is very small. Therefore, the sewing line in the middle is not very dense, with only two sewing lines. ## Step 6: Preparing for Simulation Before we can start the simulation, we need to reduce the particle diameter of the plate to 10 and reduce the conflict thickness to 1. After starting the simulation, the plate will fall down. If needed, press Ctrl + Z to return to the previous state. ### Fixing Pins Before we start the simulation, we can press W and click the plate. The position we click will create a fixed pin. To delete the fixed pin, press W and click the pin again. Now we can use the satin sewing machine to fix it to the virtual model. This function allows a point of the plate to be fixed to the virtual model. When you click, be sure to pay attention to the angle. ## Step 7: Adjusting the Plates As we add a satin sewing machine, it’s important to keep them parallel. We can narrow some plates after narrowing them. This will allow the plate to be fixed in a position near our thigh. If we add a sewing needle and it’s not symmetrical, you can adjust the position of the point on the model with the satin sewing machine. ### Finalizing the Fit At this point, be sure to pay attention to the selected point; it should show as a red dot on the virtual model. Now, the entire panel is tight against the human body. We can manually drag the panel to fix it in a more flat position. ## Step 8: Applying Fabric Next, we apply a new fabric to these two panels and increase the friction coefficient of the new fabric. This can help prevent the fabric from sliding. After adjusting the friction coefficient, we can drag a panel to see that there is significant friction. Fixing it there will prevent any sliding. ### Importance of Friction The advantage of doing this is that, for example, if we make some changes or record an animation, it can prevent issues. Since the movement of the legs is relatively large, if this edge is visible, you can sew the bottom of the skirt to the top of this edge. To make it invisible, you can sew it under this edge or apply transparency to this edge. ## Step 9: Sewing the Edge In this section, I use the line sewing tool to sew directly on this edge. The position we choose is more natural, leaning on it. After we start the simulation, we will see the effect of the pumpkin skirt will be more pronounced and a little better. ## Conclusion After completion, you can adjust the particle diameter or change the fabric properties and pressure according to your needs. ```
